label: feature
file: src/api/reports.ts

This is a request for new behaviour: today the export endpoint only supports `csv` and `xlsx` (see `SUPPORTED_FORMATS` in `src/exportUtils.ts` and the `renderExport`/`:id/export` route in `src/api/reports.ts`, which dispatches to `writeCsv`/`writeXlsx`). Adding TSV would mean adding a `tsv` writer under `src/export/` and wiring it into `renderExport` and `SUPPORTED_FORMATS`, which is a legitimate feature request (and would also fix the comma-in-description escaping issue the reporter describes, since tab-delimited output sidesteps comma collisions).

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser only splits input on "\n" (`text.split("\n")`) and never strips a
trailing "\r". Files produced by Windows tools use CRLF line endings, so each
line (including the header) ends with a stray "\r" character. That makes the
last header column come out as `description\r`, which no longer matches the
required column name `description` in `REQUIRED_COLUMNS`. `assertShape` then
reports `missingRequired`, which is exactly the "Malformed row" error, and
since it happens on the header line itself it's always reported as row 1 —
matching what's described in the issue, starting right after finance switched
to a new Windows export tool that presumably emits CRLF line endings.

The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing "\r" from each
line, or split on /\r?\n/) in `parseStatement`/`splitFields` in
`src/ingest/parser.ts`.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

The reset-password (and rollup/export) links are built from a module-level constant:

```ts
const BASE_URL = process.env.PUBLIC_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000";
```

Unlike every other setting in `src/config.ts` (DB_URL, S3_BUCKET, SMTP_HOST, JWT_SIGNING_KEY, etc.), this value isn't read through `loadConfig()`/`required()`, so there's no validation and no startup failure if `PUBLIC_URL` is missing in the deployed environment — it just silently falls back to `http://localhost:3000` and ships that URL in real emails. That matches the report exactly: the token and TTL are correct, only the host is wrong, and it reportedly started after a recent release (most likely one where `PUBLIC_URL` stopped being set, or where this template code was introduced/changed).

Fix should add a `publicUrl` field to `AppConfig` (populated via `required("PUBLIC_URL")` or similar in `config.ts`) and have `templates.ts` use `config.publicUrl` instead of reading `process.env` directly, so a missing value fails fast at startup instead of quietly defaulting to localhost in production.

label: question
file: none

No, we don't keep the original file after a successful import. Once the worker (`src/ingest/worker.ts`) finishes parsing a file and inserting the resulting transactions, it deletes the uploaded file from object storage immediately (`storage.remove(upload.key)` right after `completeJob`) — only the parsed transaction rows remain.

If an import *fails*, the original file is kept for 7 days (`FAILED_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS` in `src/ingest/worker.ts`) so the file can be inspected to diagnose the problem, then it's deleted automatically by an hourly purge job (`purgeExpiredFailedUploads`).

This is also documented in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` under "What happens to uploaded files". Nothing to fix here — just answering for your review.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

This isn't the CSV writer — it's the ingest-time dedupe logic. `dedupeKey` builds its key from `[t.date, t.amount, t.description]` only (src/ingest/dedupe.ts), so two transactions that match on those three fields but differ in currency (e.g. 10.00 EUR vs 10.00 USD) hash to the same key and are collapsed into one during `dedupe()`/`keysFor()`. Since currency was only added to transactions as of 3.2.0 (per CHANGELOG), this previously-safe key stopped being unique. The exporter in `src/export/csv.ts` only ever sees the already-deduped set, so it just faithfully prints whichever row survived ingest.

Fix should add `t.currency` to the key in `dedupeKey`.

label: feature
file: src/api/reports.ts

Report export currently only supports CSV and XLSX (see `SUPPORTED_FORMATS` in `src/exportUtils` and the `renderExport` switch in `src/api/reports.ts`, which dispatches to `writeCsv`/`writeXlsx`). Adding TSV would mean introducing a `writeTsv` writer (alongside `src/export/csv.ts`), adding `"tsv"` to `SUPPORTED_FORMATS`/`ExportFormat`, and wiring it into the `renderExport` switch and the `/reports/:id/export` endpoint. This is a reasonable ask: a tab-delimited writer would sidestep the comma-in-description escaping problem the reporter describes, so no manual CSV→TSV conversion would be needed.

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

`isRollupDue` in `src/notifications/rollup.ts` correctly computes the user's local hour via `localHour(now, tz)`, but it then calls `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)` to find the start of the user's week — and `startOfWeek` has a `// TODO: honour tz` and actually computes the week boundary purely from `now.getUTCDay()`, ignoring the time zone argument entirely.

For a time zone ahead of UTC (like `Australia/Sydney`, UTC+10/+11), local Monday 08:00 falls on *Sunday* in UTC. At that instant, `getUTCDay()` is Sunday, so the UTC-based `startOfWeek` returns the *previous* week's Monday (6 days earlier), making `now.getTime() - weekStart.getTime()` far larger than `DAY_MS`, so `isRollupDue` returns false and the email is skipped. The check only succeeds a day later (local Tuesday 08:00 Sydney time), when the UTC calendar day has caught up to Monday — which is exactly the reported one-day delay. Time zones behind or at UTC (e.g. London) don't have this mismatch between local day and UTC day at the send hour, so they're unaffected.

Fix: `startOfWeek` needs to actually honour `tz` (e.g. compute the day-of-week in the target zone) rather than relying on `getUTCDay()`.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

The reset-password (and rollup/export) links are built from a module-level
`BASE_URL` constant that falls back to `http://localhost:3000` whenever
`PUBLIC_URL` isn't set:

```ts
const BASE_URL = process.env.PUBLIC_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000";
```

Unlike every other setting (DB, SMTP, S3, auth, etc.), this value is read
directly from `process.env` here instead of going through `src/config.ts`,
and there is no corresponding field in `AppConfig`/`FileConfig` for it at
all. So if `PUBLIC_URL` isn't exported in the environment this file is run
in (e.g. a deploy/config change in last week's release), it silently falls
back to localhost instead of failing loudly or using the configured
production URL — which matches what the reporter and teammates are seeing.

Fix should add a proper `publicUrl` entry to `AppConfig` (required in
production, like `DB_URL`/`SMTP_HOST` are) and have `templates.ts` consume
`config.publicUrl` instead of reading `process.env.PUBLIC_URL` with a
silent localhost fallback.

label: question
file: none

Thanks for checking in. Per `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("What happens to uploaded files") and the implementation in `src/ingest/worker.ts`:

- On a **successful** import, the worker deletes the uploaded file from object storage right after the import completes — only the parsed transactions (in the `transactions` table) are retained, not the original file.
- If an import **fails**, the original file is kept for 7 days (`FAILED_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS` in `src/ingest/worker.ts`) so the file can be inspected/debugged, and is then removed by an hourly purge job.

So we don't retain uploaded source files beyond a short failure-debugging window; nothing to fix here.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

`parseStatement` splits the uploaded text only on `"\n"` and never strips a
trailing `"\r"` from each line. The new Windows accounting export almost
certainly writes CRLF (`\r\n`) line endings, so the header line ends up as
`"date,amount,description\r"`. After `lines[0].split(",")`, the last header
field becomes `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`.

In `assertShape`, `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some((column) => !header.includes(column))`
then finds that `"description"` is no longer in the header array (it's
`"description\r"`), so `missingRequired` is true and the function throws
`errors.rowShape` for the header itself — which is exactly the "row 1" error
being reported, even though the file opens fine in a spreadsheet (which
normalizes line endings transparently) and has the correct three columns.

The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing `\r` from each
line, or split on `/\r\n|\n/`) before parsing the header and rows in
`parseStatement`.

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

`isRollupDue` correctly computes the local hour for the recipient's time zone via `localHour`, but it also calls `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)` to check whether `now` falls within the first day of the user's week. `startOfWeek` ignores the `tz` argument entirely (see the `// TODO: honour tz` comment) and always computes the Monday-00:00 boundary in UTC.

For a user in Sydney (UTC+10/+11), local Monday 08:00 is still Sunday (UTC) for much of the day, i.e. it falls *before* the UTC week boundary that `startOfWeek` computes. So `now.getTime() - weekStart.getTime() < DAY_MS` fails at the moment local time says Monday 08:00, and the rollup isn't sent until the next qualifying tick once the UTC-based week start has caught up — effectively pushing the email to Tuesday local time. Users close to UTC (e.g. London) don't see this because their local Monday 08:00 is close enough to the UTC boundary that the check still passes.

Fixing `startOfWeek` to actually compute the week boundary in the given time zone (rather than UTC) should resolve this for users in time zones far from UTC.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The CSV writer isn't actually merging anything — the row loss happens earlier, at ingest time. `dedupeKey` in `src/ingest/dedupe.ts` builds its key from `date`, `amount`, and `description` only:

```ts
export const dedupeKey = (t: IncomingTransaction) => [t.date, t.amount, t.description].join("|");
```

Since transactions started carrying a `currency` field (3.2.0), two distinct transactions that share date/amount/description but differ only in currency (e.g. EUR vs USD) now hash to the same key. `dedupe()` treats the second one as a duplicate of the first and drops it before it's ever stored, so the exporter only ever sees one of them — nothing to merge on the CSV side.

Fix should include `currency` in `dedupeKey` (and in `keysFor`, which reuses it) so transactions that differ only by currency aren't treated as duplicates.

label: feature
file: src/exportUtils.ts

This is a request for new export functionality, not a bug. Currently `SUPPORTED_FORMATS` in `src/exportUtils.ts` only lists `"csv"` and `"xlsx"`, which is used to validate the `format` query param in `src/api/reports.ts` (`GET /reports/:id/export`), to type the schedule format, and to populate the format picker in `src/components/ExportButton.tsx`.

Adding TSV support would mean:
- adding `"tsv"` to `SUPPORTED_FORMATS` in `src/exportUtils.ts`,
- adding a `writeTsv` writer (likely `src/export/tsv.ts`, similar to `src/export/csv.ts`) that tab-delimits fields and escapes/quotes values containing tabs or newlines,
- wiring it into `renderExport` in `src/api/reports.ts`,
- updating `docs/API.md` and `README.md` to mention the new format.

This would directly solve the reporter's problem (commas in transaction descriptions breaking their CSV→TSV conversion) since a proper TSV writer only needs to escape tabs/newlines, not commas.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

The password-reset (and other) email links are built from `BASE_URL = process.env.PUBLIC_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000"` in `src/notifications/templates.ts`. There is no `publicUrl`/`PUBLIC_URL` entry in `src/config.ts`'s `AppConfig`/`loadConfig()` at all, so nothing validates or documents this variable — if `PUBLIC_URL` isn't set in the production environment (e.g. after a deploy/release that didn't carry it over), the code silently falls back to `http://localhost:3000` for every generated link, which matches exactly what's being reported.

Fix should add a proper `publicUrl` field to `AppConfig` (loaded via `required("PUBLIC_URL")` or similar, so missing config fails fast instead of silently defaulting to localhost), and have `templates.ts` use `config.publicUrl` instead of reading `process.env.PUBLIC_URL` directly.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the file strictly on `"\n"` and never strips `\r`. Windows-originated CSVs (like the new accounting export tool finance just switched to) use CRLF line endings, so each line — including the header line — ends with a trailing `\r`. That makes the last header column come out as `"description\r"` instead of `"description"`.

In `assertShape`, this fails the `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some((column) => !header.includes(column))` check for the header row itself (called with `index = 0`), which is why the error always reports "row 1" regardless of the file's actual content — it's failing on the header before any data row is even parsed. Opening the file in a spreadsheet doesn't show this because spreadsheet apps normalize line endings transparently.

Fix: normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing `\r` from each line, or split on `/\r\n|\n/`) in `parseStatement` before splitting into fields.

Nothing to fix here. Per `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` ("What happens to uploaded files") and the ingest worker (`src/ingest/worker.ts`): after a successful import, the worker deletes the uploaded file from object storage immediately. Failed uploads are retained for `FAILED_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS` (currently 7 days) to allow debugging/retry, and are then purged automatically. No raw uploaded files are kept long-term outside of that failure window.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The CSV exporter isn't at fault here — it just writes whatever transactions it's given. The actual merging happens earlier, during ingestion: `dedupeKey` in `src/ingest/dedupe.ts` builds its key from `date`, `amount`, and `description` only:

```ts
export const dedupeKey = (t: IncomingTransaction) => [t.date, t.amount, t.description].join("|");
```

Since 3.2.0 added a `currency` field to transactions, two rows that differ only by currency (e.g. same date/amount/description, one EUR and one USD) now produce the same dedupe key and are collapsed into a single transaction by `dedupe()`/`keysFor()` before export ever sees them. That's why the CSV only shows one of them.

Fix should add `t.currency` to the key used in `dedupeKey`.

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

`isRollupDue` decides whether "now" falls within the first day of the user's
week by calling `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)` and checking that less than
24h have passed since that boundary. But `startOfWeek` in `src/util/dates.ts`
has a `// TODO: honour tz` — it computes the week start purely from
`getUTCDay()`/`setUTCDate()`, ignoring the `tz` parameter entirely.

For a user in London (UTC/UTC+1), the UTC calendar day mostly coincides with
the local day, so the Monday-in-UTC boundary is close enough to the
Monday-in-local-time boundary and the rollup fires correctly. For a user in
Sydney (UTC+10/+11), local Monday begins 10–11 hours before UTC Monday does,
so the computed `weekStart` is effectively anchored to the wrong local day:
by the time `now - weekStart < DAY_MS` and `localHour == 8` both hold for
Sydney, local wall-clock time has already rolled into Tuesday. That's exactly
the "Monday email arrives Tuesday, but only for Sydney" symptom reported.

The fix belongs in `startOfWeek`, which needs to actually compute the start
of the week in the given IANA time zone (e.g. by formatting `d` into local
y/m/d via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `tz`, finding the local weekday, and
subtracting days in local time) rather than operating on UTC fields.

file: src/exportUtils.ts

This is a request for a new TSV export format alongside the existing CSV and XLSX options. The core logic lives in src/exportUtils.ts, where SUPPORTED_FORMATS, CONTENT_TYPES, and the toDelimited()/escapeField() helpers (currently hard-coded to comma delimiters) would need to be extended to support tab-delimited output, in addition to wiring it through src/api/reports.ts and src/export/scheduler.ts.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

The password reset link is built from BASE_URL, which falls back to "http://localhost:3000" whenever the PUBLIC_URL environment variable isn't set in the deployment environment. This means the production server must not have PUBLIC_URL configured (likely since last week's release, e.g. a new deploy/config that dropped the env var), so all reset emails point to localhost instead of the real public URL. Fix by ensuring PUBLIC_URL is set correctly in the production environment, and/or by failing loudly (rather than silently falling back to localhost) when it's missing in non-development environments.

Thanks for checking. Successfully imported files are removed right after processing: once the rows are inserted into the ledger, the worker deletes the original upload from storage immediately (see the `storage.remove(upload.key)` call right after `completeJob` in `src/ingest/worker.ts`).

If an import fails, the original file is kept temporarily (so it can be inspected/retried) for `FAILED_UPLOAD_RETENTION_DAYS` = 7 days, after which a background purge job deletes it automatically.

So: successful imports -> deleted immediately; failed imports -> kept up to 7 days, then deleted. Nothing is broken here, just sharing how retention currently works.

label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the uploaded text on "\n" only (`text.split("\n")`), so it doesn't strip a trailing "\r" when the file uses Windows-style CRLF line endings. The new accounting export tool on Windows likely produces CRLF files, so the last column name in the header (and the last field of every data row) ends up with a trailing "\r" attached, e.g. "description\r" instead of "description".

Because `assertShape` checks `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some((column) => !header.includes(column))`, the mangled last header column no longer matches "description", so `missingRequired` is true and an `IngestError("errors.rowShape", { row: index + 1 })` is thrown immediately while parsing the header line (index 0), which is why it always reports "row 1" regardless of the actual file contents.

The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip a trailing "\r" from each line, or split on /\r?\n/) before splitting into header/rows.

label: bug
file: src/import/dedupe.ts

The CSV writer isn't actually merging anything — the dedupe step that runs before export treats two transactions as duplicates whenever their date, amount, and description match. `dedupeKey` in the dedupe module doesn't factor in currency, so after 3.2.0 (when transactions started carrying a currency) two otherwise-identical transactions in different currencies collide on the same key and one gets dropped as a duplicate. The fix is to include `t.currency` in `dedupeKey` so transactions that only differ by currency aren't treated as the same transaction.

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

startOfWeek ignores the tz parameter (see the "TODO: honour tz" comment) and always computes the week boundary using UTC day arithmetic. For a user in Sydney (UTC+10/+11), the UTC-based week start falls on a different local calendar day than their actual Monday, so by the time localHour(now, tz) reports 08:00 locally, `now - weekStart` has already exceeded the one-day window in isRollupDue, pushing the send out to the next day (Tuesday). Users in zones close to UTC (like London) don't notice because the UTC and local week boundaries nearly coincide. Fixing startOfWeek to compute the week start in the user's local time zone should resolve this.

file: src/notifications/templates.ts

BASE_URL falls back to `http://localhost:3000` whenever the `PUBLIC_URL` environment variable isn't set (src/notifications/templates.ts:8), and `passwordResetEmail` builds the reset link from that BASE_URL. If `PUBLIC_URL` isn't configured in the production environment (or was dropped in last week's release), reset emails, weekly rollup links, and scheduled export links will all point to localhost. The fix should ensure `PUBLIC_URL` is properly set in the deployment config, and/or this code should fail loudly instead of silently falling back to localhost in non-dev environments.

Adding TSV would mean adding a new entry to SUPPORTED_FORMATS/CONTENT_TYPES, a delimiter option for toDelimited (which currently hardcodes commas), and a corresponding writer/content-type wiring in the export routes and scheduler. file: src/ingest/parser.ts

parseStatement splits the input only on "\n" (`text.split("\n")`), so a file with Windows-style CRLF line endings leaves a trailing "\r" on every line, including the header. That makes the last header column (e.g. "description\r") fail to match the expected "description" in REQUIRED_COLUMNS, so assertShape's missingRequired check fails on the very first row (the header, reported as row 1) — exactly matching the "Malformed row" error always on row 1 after finance switched to a new Windows export tool. The parser should strip/handle "\r" (e.g. split on /\r?\n/ or trim each line) before processing header and rows.

file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

The dedupeKey function only hashes date, amount, and description, so two transactions that differ only by currency (e.g. one EUR, one USD) produce the same key and are treated as duplicates. This isn't a CSV export bug (src/export/csv.ts just writes whatever rows it receives) — the rows are being merged earlier, during dedupe/ingest. The key should also include currency to avoid dropping legitimate transactions that share date, amount, and description but differ in currency.

file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input only on "\n" and never strips a trailing "\r", so it cannot handle CRLF line endings (the default for Windows-based export tools). With CRLF input, the header line ends up as e.g. "date,amount,description\r", so after splitting on "," the last header column becomes "description\r" instead of "description". Since finance switched to a new Windows accounting export tool, it's very likely now producing CRLF line endings, while the parser was only ever tested/working with LF. The fix should normalize line endings (e.g. strip trailing "\r" per line, or split on /\r?\n/) in `parseStatement`.

label: bug
file: src/util/dates.ts

The rollup scheduler (src/notifications/rollup.ts) decides when to send by calling `localHour(now, user.timezone)` and `startOfWeek(now, user.timezone)`, gating the send on `SEND_HOUR` (08:00) local time on the first day of the user's week. London (UTC+0/+1) works correctly, but Sydney (UTC+10/+11) consistently gets the email a day late, which points to an error in the timezone-offset math inside `src/util/dates.ts`'s `localHour`/`startOfWeek` implementation — likely mishandling positive (east-of-UTC) offsets when computing local date/hour boundaries, so the "Monday 08:00 local" window is being mis-detected for zones ahead of UTC and the email fires on the next tick instead.

file: src/export/scheduler.ts

The scheduler computes `nextRunAt` purely in UTC: it sets a fixed `RUN_HOUR_UTC` (06:00 UTC) and advances by whole UTC days/weeks, ignoring the report/user's `timezone` setting entirely (even though `types.ts` and the DB schema support a per-user IANA timezone). For a user in Sydney (UTC+10/+11), 06:00 UTC already falls on the next local calendar day, so a run scheduled to land on "Monday" in UTC actually lands on Tuesday local time — while London users, whose offset keeps 06:00 UTC within the same local day, see no issue. The scheduler needs to compute "Monday 00:00" (or whatever send time) in the recipient's timezone rather than assuming UTC-aligned days.

The CSV writer in `src/export/csv.ts` simply calls `toDelimited()` on the rows it is given and writes each row through verbatim — it does not merge or deduplicate anything itself. `toDelimited()` in `src/exportUtils.ts` iterates `rows` and emits one line per row using `cellValue()`, which does correctly read `row.currency` for the `currency` column (added as part of `COLUMN_ORDER` since 3.2.0).
